title: Final Bill and Patient Liability on the Hospital Account (Encounter Billing)
content:
Charges accrue on a Hospital Account (Encounter Billing) while it is pending billing, until the final bill drops the class's bill-hold days in calendar days after the service end date. A monthly-series account is billed after the last day of each service month, each month being billed separately.

## Where the final bill drops

- **Self-pay financial class.** The final bill drops to the patient: the whole net gross charges post as one self-pay final-bill liability, and the uninsured discount follows.
- **Any other financial class.** The final bill drops to the primary payer as a claim.

## What becomes the patient's liability on an insured account

When the payer adjudicates, only the amounts the payer reports as patient responsibility post as liability: deductible, coinsurance, copay, non-covered service and coverage terminated. Each posts as its own liability posting carrying the claim reference. Amounts the payer reports as a contractual obligation are never billed to the patient.

If no adjudication is received within the class's insurer no-response days of the claim's submitted date, billing reviews the account and it stays insurance pending; the patient is not billed for an unadjudicated claim.

## Closing and charges

An account closes when its patient balance reaches zero, or when the payer pays in full leaving nothing to the patient. Riverbend charges no interest and no late fees on any patient balance.

## Illustration (hypothetical remittance)

A payer adjudicates a claim reporting 300.00 deductible, 120.00 coinsurance and 2400.00 contractual obligation. Two liability postings follow on the account, 300.00 and 120.00, each carrying the claim reference; the 2400.00 is never billed to the patient.
